candidates.description: kNN-expanded upper structure proposal; intended to make sparse handles, loops, rings, or top protrusions reviewable.
View-derived points above the dense main body; useful for handles, loops, rings, or top protrusions.
Expanded multi-view foreground component; retained even when partially visible.
Union of two strong loop/handle-like components. This is a high-recall proposal for paired handles, double rings, scissor finger holes, and symmetric grasp/hook structures.
kNN-expanded small compact or high-curvature component for buttons, knobs, switches, handle joints, and thin legs.
Expanded existing weak mask prior; useful but not trusted as final GT.
kNN-expanded connected high-curvature/linear component; designed for complete handles, rings, holes, loops, lips, or similar functional structures.
kNN-expanded high-curvature/linear points near the low extreme of the x axis. Useful for handles, loops, lips, knobs, and side/end functional parts.
kNN-expanded strict high-curvature/linear component for more precise functional boundaries.
kNN-expanded checked/weak mask channel for gripper; useful when the existing prior is sparse but spatially close to a functional part.
Raw multi-view foreground component seed for precise review.
small compact or high-curvature component for buttons, knobs, switches, handle joints, and thin legs.
connected high-curvature or linear component for handles, rings, holes, lips, and thin parts.
Existing checked/weak mask channel for gripper; useful as a spatial prior, not final truth. A gripper/hand prior may overlap handles that are relevant to hook.
Raw existing weak mask prior retained for traceability.
strict high-curvature/linear component for more precise functional boundaries.
kNN-expanded smooth/planar component for suction, press, panel, door, or broad contact regions.
Compact protruding/high-curvature points; may be buttons, knobs, small handles, or switch-like regions.
Connected high-curvature/linear seed component before expansion; useful for precise boundary review.
High-curvature boundary points; may indicate edges, lips, holes, knobs, or handles.
Locally linear points; may correspond to stems, handles, rods, rings, or thin graspable structures.
High-curvature points near the high extreme of the z axis.
Linear structure near the low extreme of the x axis.
Low-curvature and planar points; potential suction or push/panel candidate.

notes: Candidate overlays are for VLM selection and human inspection only.
